narrative.overview: The page is printed matter left in warm afternoon light: cream paper, two mounted specimens, a four-color registration bar, and enough air around the objects that they read as exhibits rather than a listing. The interface is editorial and quiet; the SalaryTicker card is the loudest thing on the page, with JobPilot as a smaller companion exhibit. Warmth comes from paper, light, and ink, never from a pastel gradient pasted over a template. The page is built around one typographic gesture: a very large Song-style headline with a drawn coral underline, then two project cards that rise into view. The personal four-color mark sits in the header and footer; the product icon belongs only to the SalaryTicker card. Four colors — coral, amber, green, blue — recur as hairlines, dots, stripe segments, and the eight-ray mark. Nothing is glossy; surfaces are warm white with 1px warm borders and shadows that look like paper lifted off a desk. Motion is deliberate and low-frequency: a line-mask reveal, cards that tilt under the pointer, a slow aurora, a ticker that behaves like a clock. If the visitor has asked for reduced motion, the page becomes a still print sheet.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a subtle aurora and 5% grain, never a flat white canvas.
One oversized serif gesture per screen; the rest is quiet system type.
Four-color registration details used structurally, not as decoration.
Warm white surfaces, 1px warm borders, deep paper shadows.
Mono for measurements, labels, and the live amount; tabular numerals always.
Every motion has a state and a reduced-motion equivalent.

rules.name: The Coral Is Ink-Free Rule
rules.body: Coral #E07A5F never sets text below 32px. Small coral text uses #B4533C; cream text never sits on light coral.

rules.name: The Money Is Green Rule
rules.body: The amount is always money-green with tabular numerals. Demo data carries the amber 演示数据 badge on the same panel; never present a number as real pay.

rules.name: The Serif Carries the Voice Rule
rules.body: Display type is for the headline, the tagline, the About quote, and the poetry of the page. Buttons, labels, amounts, and controls never use the display face.

rules.name: The Number Is Tabular Rule
rules.body: Money, time, progress, and version numbers use tabular numerals so a changing value never reflows.

rules.name: The Paper Not Glass Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are opaque warm paper. Blur appears only where content moves beneath a control and must stay readable.

rules.name: The Lift Then Settle Rule
rules.body: Hover states lift by 6px at most and return to rest; no perpetual bobbing except the miniature window’s 7s float and the aurora.

dos: Do use warm paper fields and 1px warm borders before adding another shadow.
Do keep coral for lines, dots, the period, the cursor, and graphics; use coral-deep for small coral text.
Do keep the four-color stripe and the eight-ray mark as recurring registration details.
Do use the display serif only for the headline, the taglines, and the quote; use sans for controls and mono for data.
Do label every demo amount with 演示数据 and keep the live ticker tabular.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion result and every card a keyboard focus ring.
Do keep each project card a single link; put the accessible new-tab/demo note in aria-describedby.
Do keep SalaryTicker as the featured card and JobPilot as the smaller companion; the hierarchy is the portfolio.
donts: Don't put cream text on #E07A5F or use coral for small body text.
Don't add glass panels, gradient text, neon, or a generic SaaS hero/three-equal-cards layout.
Don't invent a third project, JobPilot metrics, additional social links, or a portrait.
Don't claim JobPilot has a domain or HTTPS before it does; keep 域名待定 / 在线预览.
Don't animate layout properties, run the WebGL shader when reduced motion is requested, or load Three.js in the entry bundle.
Don't loop the card sheen; it is one 0.9s pass per pointer enter.
Don't introduce additional kickers/eyebrows beyond the two brief-mandated labels (hero eyebrow and section labels).
Don't use pure white as a page field; it belongs only inside the app screenshot and raised paper.
